title: Toad in the Hole
subtitle: Pork sausages baked in a crisp Yorkshire pudding batter
excerpt: Good pork sausages roasted in a smoking-hot tin, then submerged in Yorkshire pudding batter and baked until the pudding billows up and browns around the sausages. A British weeknight classic.

recipe.sourceNotes: Toad in the hole is one of the oldest British baked dishes, with recipes appearing in cookbooks from the eighteenth century. The name is thought to refer to the sausages peering out from the batter like toads emerging from holes in the ground. It was originally made with various meats including kidneys, mutton, and beef; pork sausages became the standard version in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries as they were widely available and cheap. The batter is essentially the same as Yorkshire pudding batter: milk, eggs, and flour in roughly equal parts by weight, cooked in very hot fat. The batter must rest for at least 30 minutes before cooking, and the fat must be smoking hot when the batter is poured in: this is what creates the dramatic rise and the crisp exterior.

recipeTools.notes: A medium roasting tin, about 30 x 20 cm.

content.text: Rest the batter for at least 30 minutes. The fat in the tin must be smoking hot when the batter goes in: this is not optional and is the single most important step. Do not open the oven during baking or the pudding will collapse. The batter should sizzle dramatically when it hits the hot fat. Serve immediately: the pudding deflates as it cools.
Make the batter: whisk together the flour, eggs, milk, and salt until completely smooth with no lumps. Rest for at least 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Add the oil to the roasting tin and heat in the oven for 10 minutes. Add the sausages and roast for 15 minutes until starting to brown. The fat must be smoking hot.

Working quickly, pour the batter around the sausages: it should sizzle immediately. Add the thyme if using. Return to the oven immediately. Do not open the oven for 25 minutes. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the batter is deeply golden and well risen. Serve immediately with onion gravy and mustard.
